base_properties.topic_domain: political linguistics / state formation / commitment systems

stakeholders.name: turkish_state_bureaucracy
stakeholders.situation: Drafted the Alphabet Law (No. 1351, November 1928), set the fifteen-month transition deadline, ran the Millet Mektepleri adult-literacy campaign with attendance fines, controlled school curricula, state presses, and the civil registry's conversion to Latin-script records. Collects standardized administration, a legible national archive, and curricular authority over written Turkish. Exit is not meaningful: it authored the rule and staffs every enforcement organ.

stakeholders.name: new_literate_class
stakeholders.situation: Entered school after 1928 and learned to read and write exclusively in the new alphabet; staffed the expanding ministries, village institutes, teaching corps, and professions. Holds the gatekeeping position over official written culture that the older script-literate class lost. Mobility runs through state employment and party patronage; leaving the country or the sector forfeits the advantage.

stakeholders.name: domestic_printing_industry
stakeholders.situation: Converts plants to Latin typefaces and retrains compositors at one-time cost, then operates in a captive, standardized national market with guaranteed state printing contracts. Competitors holding Arabic-script type and stock see their inventories devalued. Switching to foreign markets is limited by language and scale.

stakeholders.name: arabic_script_literate_class
stakeholders.situation: Adults literate in Ottoman Turkish script — clerks, teachers, poets, merchants — wake up functionally illiterate when the deadline passes: their credentials, ledgers, correspondence, and professional standing lose their medium. Retraining through night schools is partial and slow; declining to retrain means withdrawal from public writing. Their erudition is bound up with who they take themselves to be, so starting over as pupils in middle age is not a neutral cost.

stakeholders.name: islamic_religious_establishment
stakeholders.situation: Preachers, jurisprudents, and Sufi authorities whose learning and authority rest on Arabic-script texts — Qur'an, commentaries, fiqh, Ottoman archives. The script change, alongside tighter regulation of religious instruction, cuts direct textual access for congregations and pushes unauthorized Qur'an courses underground; the state trains a parallel Latin-script religious cadre under the Diyanet. Refusal means losing the flock to the state-sanctioned cadre; accommodation means teaching in a script that severs the tradition's chain of transmission.

stakeholders.name: rural_adult_learners
stakeholders.situation: Village adults conscripted into compulsory literacy courses, fined for absence, studying after fieldwork hours under campaign deadlines. Gains uneven literacy; cannot refuse without penalty; migration to cities is possible but costly and leaves the fine and the stigma behind.

stakeholders.name: ottoman_script_publishers
stakeholders.situation: Printers, type founders, and booksellers holding Arabic-script plant and inventory. Their trade is criminalized and then starved by regulation; they would have pressed for a gradual dual-script transition and compensation, but they are not part of the policy conversation — their objections surface only in closed chambers, if at all. Their capital is script-specific and cannot be resold.

stakeholders.name: script_reform_historians
stakeholders.situation: Comparative scholars of literacy, nationalism, and script reform who assess outcomes, attribution, and identity effects across countries and decades. Hold no enforcement role and bear none of the settlement's costs; their stake is interpretive.

six_questions.coordination_function: Provides a single phonetic, internationally compatible orthography for Turkish, solving once and centrally: mass-teachable literacy, standardized state record-keeping, machine-set printing, and notational compatibility with Western science and technology.
six_questions.transfer_function: Moves written-culture gatekeeping and administrative standardization gains to the state and its newly trained literate cadre; moves the capital of existing Arabic-script literacy (credentials, correspondence, professional standing, textual access) into devaluation; moves adult time and compliance (course attendance, fines) from citizens to the campaign.
six_questions.absent_voices: Arabic-script literati, the ulema, and Ottoman-script publishers would have objected — for gradual dual-script transition, retention of Arabic-script religious instruction, compensation for devalued trades — but by 1928 the opposition press was closed, independent deputies purged, and the conversation confined to the reform's own cadres; ordinary citizens were consulted through orchestrated acclamation rather than representation.
six_questions.disappearance_rationale: Overnight removal of the Latin-script mandate would force reorganization of schooling, state records, the print economy, and eventually digital infrastructure around either restored Arabic script or a dual-script regime; the new literate class's credentials, the bureaucracy's archive, and the entire post-1928 textual corpus would need re-mediation — visible arrangements depend on the settlement.
six_questions.founding_problem: In 1928 roughly nine in ten Turks could not read: the Arabic script, adapted poorly to Turkish vowels, took years to master, blocked mass schooling, tied the Republic's written culture to an Ottoman-Islamic scribal class, and severed easy contact with Western technical literature.
six_questions.founding_problem_corroboration: Corroborated from outside the benefiting parties: UNESCO and Turkish Statistical Institute literacy series show the mass-illiteracy barrier resolved within two generations; contemporaneous assessments by foreign educators (American and European mission reports on the Millet Mektepleri) attested both the initial deficit and its closure; comparative historical demography shows literacy also rising in polities that retained Arabic script, confirming the original barrier was not permanent. No beneficiary-party attestation is relied on for the status claim.

commentary.narrative_context:
Between 1928 and the mid-1950s the Turkish Republic replaced the Arabic script with a modified Latin alphabet by law, enforced through a fifteen-month transition deadline, compulsory adult-literacy courses with attendance fines, state monopoly over approved textbooks and presses, and regulation of Arabic-script religious instruction. This story instantiates ONE reading of the contested orthographic kernel — the modernization_reading, which holds that the settlement enabled technological and scientific modernization while preserving Turkish linguistic identity — and authors nothing about the sibling readings inside the constraint itself. The epsilon referent is the standing arrangement under contest (the enforced Latin-script settlement as it operated 1928-1958), assessed by this reading's own lights: transition coercion, devalued script capital, and foreclosed alternatives count as costs; delivered literacy and standardization count as coordination. The reading's endorsed counterfactual is NOT the referent. Claim and metrics are independent authored facts: the claimed type is what this reading's seat holds structurally true; the metrics describe the arrangement's actual operation.

KEY AGENTS (by structural relationship):
- turkish_state_bureaucracy: agenda-setter and principal collector (institutional/arbitrage)
- new_literate_class: secondary beneficiary (organized/mobile)
- domestic_printing_industry: incidental beneficiary (moderate/constrained)
- arabic_script_literate_class: primary bearer of costs (moderate/identity_locked)
- islamic_religious_establishment: bearer of costs (organized/identity_locked)
- rural_adult_learners: bearer of costs (powerless/trapped)
- ottoman_script_publishers: excluded voice (moderate/trapped)
- script_reform_historians: analytical observer (analytical/analytical)
commentary.logic_rationale: Base extractiveness is moderate (0.44 at interval end) and DECLINING across the series (0.66 at the 1928 coercion peak, when the deadline passed and roughly a million Arabic-script literates lost their medium overnight, down to 0.44 as the settlement consolidated into ordinary infrastructure): the same structure that delivered mass-teachable literacy also devalued existing script capital, compelled adult labor, and foreclosed alternatives, but the asymmetric burden was heaviest at the transition and attenuated as new cohorts grew up inside the settlement. Suppression (0.45) is the raw structural property — legal foreclosure of Arabic-script instruction and publication persisted even after active policing relaxed — and is deliberately NOT conflated with the suppression_requirement series, which traces enforcement CAPACITY: heavy at the start (inspectors, fines, campaign police, 0.72) and decaying monotonically (0.33 by 1958) as compliance became self-sustaining and the enforcement machinery was stood down. Theater ratio rises gently (0.12 to 0.32) as anniversary ceremonies and commemorative literacy rituals accumulate around a function that remains mostly real — well below the proxy-replacement threshold. Accessibility collapse is 0.70: Arabic-script literacy did not vanish (private religious channels, diaspora publishing, and household copies of Ottoman texts persisted) but was legally and socially marginalized. Resistance is 0.48: passive non-attendance, quiet retention of old-script correspondence, and periodic unrest, but no sustained open movement — partly because the payer coalition (old literati plus ulema) had already been politically broken by the 1925 Maintenance of Order regime and the closure of the opposition press BEFORE the script reform landed, which is itself part of the constraint's enforcement history. The three metric series share one time grid (seven points, 1928-1958) so no row is backfilled. Dynamics are monotonic decay, not cyclical; no intermittent-reinforcement mechanism is posited.
commentary.perspectival_gap: The seats compute differently from the same structural data. From the agenda-setter seat (state bureaucracy), the settlement is coordination it built, paid for, and willingly maintains — a rope-shaped experience with administrative dividends. From the identity_locked payer seats (Arabic-script literati, ulema), the identical structure operated as abrupt dispossession: their literacy, authority, and self-concept were denominated in a medium the state invalidated, with no exit that did not pass through self-abandonment — the most extraction-amplified experience in the story. From the new_literate_class seat, the settlement is opportunity plus mild obligation. From the trapped rural seat, it is compulsion with uneven reward. The engine computes these per-seat classifications from power, exit, and directional position; the authored claim adjudicates none of them.
commentary.directionality_logic: Beneficiary/victim declarations drive the derivation. The state bureaucracy sits nearest the beneficiary pole (designer-collector, d near 0.05-0.1); the new literate class slightly above it (collects gatekeeping rents but bears career dependence, d near 0.15); the printing industry higher still because its benefit arrived only after absorbing one-time conversion costs (d near 0.2). The Arabic-script literate class sits near the full-target pole (d near 0.85): identity_locked exit amplifies its position beyond what a mobile agent with the same losses would occupy. The Islamic establishment is similar (d near 0.8) with a generational horizon that spreads the loss across its transmission chain. Rural adult learners are trapped and powerless (d near 0.75) but their absolute stake per capita is smaller. National spatial scope adds the engine's modest verification-scaling to effective extraction for the target seats. No directionality overrides are authored: the structural derivation from roles, power, and exit options reproduces the true relationships without correction.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The founding problem — mass illiteracy rooted in a script ill-suited to Turkish — was substantially resolved within the interval, corroborated by literacy series and foreign-educator reports from outside the benefiting parties; the arrangement nonetheless persists, having acquired new functions (global technical compatibility, carriage of national identity). This is the classic completed-mandate profile, and the classification apparatus prevents two symmetrical errors. Reading the settlement as pure coordination (rope) erases the identifiable payers — the devalued literati, the severed ulema, the fined villagers — whose costs rode the same structure that delivered the dividend. Reading it as pure extraction (snare) erases the real, widely shared coordination good that survives honest accounting and that no payer sought to abolish once acquired. The dead-problem-plus-world_rearranges mismatch flags the arrangement for zombie investigation, but the cross-check runs against the low theater ratio and the live residual functions: the flag should resolve as mandate-completed-not-theatrical unless later measurements show ceremonial maintenance displacing function. The identity-lock analysis matters here: if the fused identity frame of the old literati had broken — had a bilingual mediation market emerged, for instance — their exit options would have shifted toward constrained-mobile and their effective burden would have fallen sharply without any change in the settlement itself.
commentary.kernel_context: This story instantiates the modernization_reading of the orthographic_kernel — the contested commitment that a polity's script settlement adjudicates legitimate written Turkish. The sibling readings are continuity_reading (Arabic script preserves Ottoman cultural continuity and the Islamic textual tradition) and rupture_reading (the change was deliberate cultural rupture to sever the Ottoman/Islamic past and create a new national identity). This file authors ONLY the modernization reading as a clean, epsilon-invariant constraint over the shared referent (the enforced 1928 settlement); the siblings are separate files with their own epsilon, beneficiary sets, and types, linked through network.affects_constraints. The readings coexist as live justifications held by different factions beneath a single enforced artifact; none logically forecloses another, because they differ on evaluative criteria and intent attributions rather than on mutually exclusive ontological placements.

omegas.question: This constraint is the modernization_reading of the orthographic_kernel; how would the classification shift if the same enforced settlement were instantiated under the continuity_reading or the rupture_reading?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Author the sibling stories against the identical referent (the enforced 1928-1958 settlement) and compare epsilon, beneficiary/victim sets, and computed types across the three files.
omegas.impact: The continuity_reading would likely raise epsilon by counting severed heritage-text access as a cost borne by all post-1928 generations, enlarging the victim set beyond the transition cohorts; the rupture_reading would raise epsilon further and recast the state elite as deliberate identity engineers, potentially shifting the computed type toward snare. Divergence across the triplet is the measurement; convergence would suggest the readings collapse into one constraint.
omegas.description: Committer-frame indexicality: classification is conditional on which reading of the orthographic kernel this story instantiates.

omegas.question: How much of the observed literacy expansion is attributable to the script change itself versus the simultaneous expansion of schooling, state capacity, and economic growth?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Comparative cohort analysis against Muslim-majority polities that retained Arabic script (which also raised literacy, with lag), plus within-Turkey cohort discontinuities at the 1928 schooling boundary.
omegas.impact: Low attribution undermines the reading's coordination claim and shifts explanatory weight toward identity-engineering accounts, moving the constraint's structure toward the rupture_reading's shape; high attribution stabilizes the tangled_rope reading and the moderate epsilon.
omegas.description: Attribution of the settlement's headline benefit between script mechanics and confounded modernization inputs.

omegas.question: Did Turkish linguistic identity survive because of the Latin settlement (phonetic fit, vernacular standardization) or merely despite the rupture it inflicted on the textual tradition?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Longitudinal sociolinguistic indicators: vernacular vitality, language-loyalty survey series, and comparison with the identity trajectories of Arabized-Ottoman successor states.
omegas.impact: If survival is attributable to mechanisms independent of the script, the reading's second premise (preservation) loses causal warrant and the constraint's justification narrows to the modernization premise alone, weakening the coordination-function gate.
omegas.description: Whether the identity-preservation half of the reading's claim is causally supported or incidental.

omegas.question: How large was the population whose literacy capital was devalued at the 1928 deadline, and what was the welfare cost of the transition to them?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: 1927 census literacy microdata, cohort wage and literacy trajectories across the deadline, and contemporary reports on Millet Mektepleri enrollment and completion rates.
omegas.impact: Sizes the payer seats' effective burden: a small devalued cohort supports lower effective extraction than the structural declarations suggest; a large one raises it and strengthens the asymmetric-extraction gate.
omegas.description: Magnitude of the one-time devaluation of Arabic-script human capital.

omegas.question: Is the adjudicating authority for the orthographic kernel the state lineage (Ministry of Education and the Turkish Language Association transmitting the 1928 settlement by institutional descent), or the practitioner community of teachers, writers, and editors whose working practice IS the operative standard?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Trace adjudication events — spelling-commission rulings, dictionary editions, textbook approvals — and determine whether state organs decide by fiat or ratify practitioner consensus ex post.
omegas.impact: Under the practice framing, authority_grounding moves from lineage to practice and the interpretation layer becomes the profession itself; the kernel-level commitment-system pattern may shift without changing the constraint's type or epsilon. Signals guiding the current choice: the settlement's adjudication organs are state-chartered and their legitimacy claims invoke the founding act.
omegas.description: CS-framing under-determination: two coherent authority framings for the same kernel with different cs_structure outputs.

network.dual_formulation_note: 'The Turkish script reform' is a colloquial label covering three structurally distinct constraints — one per reading of the orthographic_kernel. Each reading authors its own epsilon over the SAME referent (the enforced Latin-script settlement): this modernization_reading counts transition coercion and devalued script capital against delivered coordination (epsilon 0.44, tangled_rope); the continuity_reading counts severed textual-heritage access across all post-1928 generations (higher epsilon, enlarged victim set); the rupture_reading counts deliberate identity engineering (highest epsilon, ideological-extractor framing of the state elite). The stories are linked as a constraint family, not merged; no single story averages across readings, per the epsilon-invariance principle. Upstream/downstream: the modernization reading's delivered-results record is routinely cited as evidence AGAINST the continuity reading's claims, giving this file a evidentiary-pressure edge toward its siblings.
